extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). Completing these tasks requires fine-grained, deep visual understanding and compositional reasoning.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research, Redmond
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao. MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MathVista incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering (MathQA) datasets and 19 VQA datasets. In addition, three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created. For MathQA datasets, each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates, yielding 4,949 VQA-format examples. Expert annotators manually labeled these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning using majority voting, finalizing 2,739 examples. The three new datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data sources include 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets. MathQA datasets include sources for geometry problem solving, math word problems with visual contexts, and textbook question answering on college curricula. VQA datasets were reviewed from more than 70 datasets, selecting 19 that contain math-related instances and are publicly available. New datasets include IQTest (228 examples from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms), FunctionQA (400 examples emphasizing functional plots and algebraic reasoning), and PaperQA (107 examples from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Papers released in August 2023 were used for PaperQA dataset collection.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning. Examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. The dataset was divided into two subsets: testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples). A sampling strategy was adopted to ensure testmini closely resembles the distribution of the whole set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three expert annotators manually labeled VQA examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. For the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and further refined through a rigorous review process. A two-step process was employed: initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. Examples in MathVista are annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and mathematical reasoning types.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom annotation tool was developed, as illustrated in the paper (Figure 23 in §D.3 and Figure 22).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The Fleiss Kappa score was used to conduct an inter-annotator agreement analysis among three annotators. The analysis yielded a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating a substantial level of consistency among the annotators. Among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in the annotated answers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. For automatic annotation of mathematical reasoning categories, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations have the exact same set of reasoning types, while 98.79% of individual labels are identical.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three annotators per item for manual labeling of mathematical reasoning involvement. For the newly created datasets, three reviewers independently annotated each dataset.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields annotated the three new datasets. For human performance baseline, eligible annotators from Amazon Mechanical Turk must have a satisfactory annotating history, successfully pass qualification examples, and possess a high school degree or higher.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules were used for automatic selection of mathematical problems from VQA datasets. EasyOCR was used for OCR text detection. Multimodal Bard was used to generate image captions for augmented LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into testmini (1,000 examples) for model development validation and test (5,141 examples) for standard evaluation. Answer labels for test will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets and refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes questions about celebrities and their ages. Some images contain people, though Multimodal Bard restricted responses to images of people in some cases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to the heterogeneity of sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions, including languages such as Chinese and Persian. GPT-4V's self-verification is weaker for non-English tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It can be used for testing and validation of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs). The benchmark is intended to facilitate the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks. Use cases include: Training, Testing, Validation.
